newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Nera has slightly lower Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Nera has slightly lower Q1 profits.

text.p: Norwegian telecommunications group Nera ASA said on Thursday first-quarter pre-tax profits fell 0.75 percent to 26.4 million crowns because of reduced sales of transmission systems.
But extensive sales of the new satellite telephone Nera WorldPhone boosted sales for mobile satellite communications, the company said in a statement.
Nera, a small Bergen-based company, has become a global player in the niche markets for satellite communication and transmission systems.

Operating revenues in the first quarter fell to 540.9 million crowns from 628.5 million, operating results shrank to 29.8 million from 35.3 million but Earnings Per Share were fixed at 1.53 crowns, up from 1.52 crowns in the corresponding year-ago period.
Nera president Asbjoern Birkeland said the expansion of Nera's market organisation would gradually boost volumes.
"We have focused on establishing a local presence in a number of countries, and experience shows that it takes time before this results in new orders," he said in the statement.
"As an example, we established an office in the Philippines last year, while the first two contracts were signed in the first quarter of this year."
The decline in revenue in the first quarter was seen as a temporary departure from a long-term positive trend.
"The prerequisites for long-term growth in the telecommunications market remain unchanged," Birkeland said.
Chairman of the board Frode Botnevik told a news conference the company expected second-quarter profits not to deviate much from the second quarter of 1996.
Nera, which was listed on the Oslo Bourse in January 1995, had pre-tax profits of 29.8 million crowns in the second quarter of 1996.
